report.source_text: On neurological examination, the patient showed normal muscular strength in the upper and lower extremities with diffusely brisk reflexes. A sensory deficit level was noted at T5–T6 with diminished pinprick and temperature sensation, loss of vibratory sensation and impaired proprioception on the left side of the body. Plantar responses were in extension bilaterally. The patient had a wide-based cautious gait with a positive Romberg sign.

report.source_text: As presented in table 1, the laboratory study showed normal thrombocytes, coagulation study and D-dimer level. Both IgM and IgG for COVID-19 were positive. Myeloneuropathy laboratory results such as copper and vitamin B12 were within the reference range. Autoimmune tests and hepatic viral study were also negative. We also investigated potential thrombophilia using homocysteine and antiphospholipid antibodies, which were all within the normal range. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis via lumbar puncture did not show abnormalities. Nerve conduction studies and electromyography of the upper and lower limbs were within normal limits. CT of the chest showed no abnormalities related to COVID-19 infection.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her early 30s with recent COVID-19 infection (2 weeks prior) presented with acute neurological syndrome characterized by severe headache, bilateral tinnitus, blurry vision, nausea, and left-sided sensory disturbance with lower body involvement, constipation, and voiding difficulties. Neurological examination revealed a sensory level at T5-T6 with left-sided loss of pinprick, temperature, vibration, and proprioception, bilateral Babinski signs, and gait disturbance with positive Romberg sign, consistent with transverse myelitis. MRI brain and MR venography demonstrated partial thrombosis of the left transverse sinus (cerebral venous thrombosis) with small atypical bilateral frontal foci of vascular origin, but no signal abnormalities in the spinal cord (MRI-negative myelitis). CSF analysis showed no abnormalities. Laboratory studies revealed normal coagulation parameters, D-dimer, and thrombophilia workup, with positive COVID-19 serology (IgM and IgG), supporting postinfectious etiology. The patient was treated with enoxaparin 60 mg subcutaneously twice daily for 10 days followed by oral rivaroxaban 20 mg daily for cerebral venous thrombosis, and intravenous dexamethasone 16 mg daily for 5 days for transverse myelitis. At 3-month follow-up, the patient demonstrated significant clinical improvement with only mild residual numbness on the left lower extremity.
